root_idea.summary: The evidence presents نُون chiefly as a concrete name for a great fish or whale, with related naming in the expression Dhū al-Nūn.
root_idea.development: The whale designation appears in possessive names: Dhū al-Nūn is Jonah's Quranic epithet, while Classical Arabic also records it as the name of a sword, apparently by comparison with the nūn.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized classical citation form نُون rather than the inflected Quranic surface form.

senses.usage_conditions: Used as an isolated letter in the Quranic opening expression ن وَالْقَلَمِ.

senses.definition: A great fish or whale; in Dhū al-Nūn, the creature associated with Jonah.
senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in the possessive epithet ذُو النُّونِ; the lexical explanation identifies it as the whale that swallowed Jonah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a sword belonging to al-Ḥārith ibn Ẓālim.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name expression, apparently based on a comparison with the nūn or whale; it is not a general word meaning “sword.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dimple in the chin of a young child.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately headed Classical Arabic noun for this anatomical feature.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Defines نَوْنَةٌ as a young child's chin dimple.

cautions: The sole supplied QAC occurrence is the inflected form in Dhū al-Nūn; the letter sense is explicitly supported by Quran-focused lexical evidence but has no separate supplied QAC occurrence in this packet.
